one_liner: Buy classified and unclassified IT services for DISA as a federal contracting officer's specialist: plan acquisitions, issue solicitations, evaluate proposals, negotiate, award and administer contracts.
fit_summary: This is a technical GS-1102 contracting job that requires at least a year of hands-on procurement work (pre-/post-award actions, cost/price analysis, or writing PWS/acquisition plans), plus a bachelor's degree and SCI eligibility. Daniel's IEM consulting and policy knowledge help with the client-advisor side, but unless Daniel actually did proposal pricing, contract administration, or procurement documentation at IEM, the specialized experience requirement likely isn't met. Any real proposal, pricing, or contract-management work at IEM is the only path to qualifying, most plausibly at GS-11.
eligibility: Open to the public under DoD Direct Hire Authority (5 USC 9905); no status needed, and veterans' preference does not apply.
Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution is mandatory, and you must upload transcripts with the application or you are disqualified.

GS-11 requires one year of experience equivalent to GS-09 in basic pre-award/post-award procurement functions or routine price/cost analysis. Alternatively, three years of graduate education in business, law, economics, or a similar field can substitute at GS-11 only.
The position requires Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access, which means a Top Secret background investigation.
Higher grades need more: GS-12 requires independently awarding contracts or writing PWS/market research/acquisition plans/J&As, and GS-13 requires cradle-to-grave Federal procurement experience.
strategy: Apply at GS-11 only. Daniel likely lacks the independent award authority needed for GS-12 or GS-13.

Inventory IEM work honestly for anything contract-related: proposal pricing, labor-category costing, task order management, invoicing and deliverable tracking, subcontractor oversight, or drafting SOW/PWS language for government clients. Describe that work in the posting's terms.
State the specialized experience inside the resume body, as the posting requires. Keep it within two pages, with dates, hours per week, and the GS-09-level procurement duties stated plainly.

Present the client-facing consulting work as 'business advisor to mission partners' and the government-client work as familiarity with the Federal acquisition lifecycle. Do not claim warrants or awards Daniel didn't make.
Upload college transcripts with the application. The posting closes 12/2/2026, and direct-hire announcements can close early or cut off at an applicant cap, so apply early.

If Daniel doesn't qualify, look for GS-1102 trainee or intern programs (DoD acquisition development programs, DAU-linked entry roles) at GS-7/9, or for 0301/0089 emergency-management roles that match the IEM background better.
resume_bullets: Supported [number] [federal/state/local] government contracts valued at [$amount] at IEM, tracking deliverables, invoices, and modifications for post-award contract administration [hours/week].
Developed cost proposals and labor-category pricing for [number] responses to government solicitations, performing price analysis to [describe outcome you can document].
Drafted [SOW/PWS/market research] sections for [client] [type of project] requirements, coordinating with program staff on acquisition planning and schedules.
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would determine whether a proposed price is fair and reasonable.
Describe a time you advised a client on a requirement that was unclear or kept changing. How did you get to a usable package on schedule?
What experience do you have with the FAR/DFARS, and how have you applied policy to an acquisition decision?
How would you handle a mission partner pressuring you to skip a procurement step to meet a deadline?
watch_outs: Specialized procurement experience cannot be waived, and Daniel's known background may not meet it.
The SCI clearance requirement means a lengthy Top Secret investigation.
Fort Meade is roughly a 60+ mile commute from Manassas. Telework is offered but not full remote.
